title: Chapter 3 — Rain and Raid
description: The first big rain, the first Task Force raid, Commander Bassey, and the first bribe.

cards.title: Day {stat:day}
cards.text: The sky over Iyana-Wahala turns the colour of an old pot. Then it falls.

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: Rain! Shoki in the rain! Passengers dey pay double for umbrella and complain triple! Na blessing!

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Rain na agbero's enemy. Drivers no dey stop, passengers no dey wait, and your energy go drain like gutter. Rule number eight: in rain, collect fast and chop early.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: (She runs past with a nylon over her head and drops a second one on you.) Cover your head. If you catch cold, who go owe me money?

beats.objective: Rainy day hustle. FEE RUN at the Back Side, stay dry, keep your energy up. (Something is coming at midday.)

cards.title: "LETS CLEAN UP!"
cards.text: A green van slides through the puddles. Out steps a man with a stomach like a promise and a baton like a threat.

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: Good afternoon, Iyana-Wahala! I am Commander Hezekiah Bassey of the Lagos Environmental and Traffic Sanitation Task Force. LETS! Clean! Up!

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: This Back Side is an illegal collection point. You. New face. You know the penalty for illegal collection, obstruction and loitering with intent to loiter?

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (whispering) Him no want arrest you. Him want breakfast. The question na: which breakfast you fit afford?

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: Talk now. My van get space.

options.text: "I no do anything. Arrest me if you wan."

options.lockedText: Professor no go stick neck out for you yet

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: Good. Very good. You see how environmental sanitation dey work? Everybody clean. Especially my pocket.

variants.text: Professor... you and your boys. Okay. Today I no see anybody. But next time, the new boy go pay his own sanitation.

cards.title: Task Force Station
cards.text: Your first night in a cell. It smells of rain, pepper and somebody's very old sardine.

beats.speaker: bassey
beats.text: You think say I like this work? I get daughter for JSS2. Her school fees dey wait for me like this cell dey wait for you. Everybody for this Lagos dey pay somebody.

options.text: "Your daughter go make you proud one day, sir."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In the morning, they let you go with ₦2,000 less and one new enemy... or one strange new friend.

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: You don see Bassey! The man stomach na Task Force headquarters. Everything wey dem seize dey go inside.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Bassey na person too. Corrupt person, but person. Remember am. One day, the person go matter more than the corruption.

variants.text: You talk rubbish give Bassey? Ehn. That one go follow you like shadow. Shadow no dey forget, and shadow no dey collect bribe.
You run from Task Force on your second week? Hmm. The street go respect you. Bassey go remember you. Both are dangerous.

beats.speaker: sunday
beats.text: Ehen, before I forget. Bíọ́dún say him conductor don waka. Him need somebody for tomorrow. Somebody with mouth and leg. I tell am say I know one JJC...

beats.title: End of Chapter 3 — Rain and Raid
beats.summary: Task Force heat {stat:policeHeat}. Bribes paid {stat:bribesPaid}. Arrests {stat:arrests}. Tomorrow: conductor work.
